en.title: Largest Group Sharing a Common Digit
en.description:
Given n two-digit positive integers. Select as many array elements as possible such that all of them contain some common decimal digit. The same value at different positions can be selected separately; a number whose tens and units digits are equal still counts as one element. Find the maximum number of elements that can be selected.

This problem uses the standard input/output format compiled by CSWork; the algorithmic rules correspond to the source problem, and the examples and test data are written by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100); the second line contains n integers (10 ≤ numbers[i] ≤ 99).
en.explanation: In example 1, you can choose 52, 25, 52, 55, which all contain the digit 5, so the answer is 4; the repeated 52 comes from different array positions.
hints: For each digit 0..9, count how many array elements it appears in. For each number, add one for its tens digit, and add one for its units digit only if it differs from the tens digit. The largest count is the answer.
